claims.text: GDACS's flood event report for Thailand (GDACS ID FL 1104122, GLIDE FL-2026-000158-THA), covering an 18 August-27 September 2026 window, records 4 deaths and 169 people displaced nationwide, with an overall Green alert level (low humanitarian impact).

Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt declared all 50 of the capital's districts flood-disaster areas on 26 September 2026, after nearly 300mm of rain fell on the city over 48 hours; the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration warned motorists to avoid more than 20 flood-affected roads and advised residents to move vehicles to higher ground.

As of 25 September 2026, flooding was reported to be affecting 11,796 households (37,036 people) across 38 districts, 143 sub-districts and 596 villages in 12 Thai provinces, per Thailand's Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM), which also issued a Cell Broadcast alert warning that Bangkok canal water levels had reached critical stage and were continuing to rise.

As of 27 September 2026, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration had established more than 200 shelters across the city with about 4,200 people evacuated into them; Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said flooding should recede once the rain subsides, as city officials work to drain floodwaters, with more thunderstorms forecast over the weekend before tapering off Monday.

GDACS's flood event report for Thailand (GDACS ID FL 1104122, GLIDE FL-2026-000158-THA, episode 52, reporting window extended to 18 August-28 September 2026) records 'Death: 6' (up from 4) and 'Displaced: 569' (up from 169); overall alert level remains Green (low humanitarian impact).

Nation Thailand, citing Thailand's Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM) 6am situation report of 29 September 2026: flooding remained active across 29 provinces and all 50 districts of Bangkok, affecting more than 2,602,309 people in 940,300 households, with the cumulative death toll since 16 September risen to 23; Samut Prakan (124,678 affected households) and Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (13,971 households) were among the worst-hit provinces.

CGTN (1 October 2026): floodwaters were receding in Bangkok and easing across most regions, though 29 provinces plus Bangkok still had active flooding; the cumulative national death toll had risen to 24 since mid-September, with more than 1.12 million households (about 3.19 million people) affected and roughly 1.71 million rai (about 273,600 hectares) of land still submerged nationwide. A government spokesperson said the water situation 'remains manageable,' while authorities warned of possible renewed flooding from 4-6 October as dam releases were expected to raise riverside water levels by about 80cm.

GDACS's flood event report for Thailand (GDACS ID FL 1104122, GLIDE FL-2026-000158-THA, episode 57, reporting window extended to 18 August-3 October 2026) records 'Death: 6' (unchanged) and 'Displaced: 627' (up from 569); overall alert level remains Green (low humanitarian impact). The report's narrative states that authorities in Thailand reported flooding in Ratchaburi Province from late September 2026.

IFRC and Thai Red Cross's 'Thailand: Flood - 09-2026 - Heavy rainfall caused flooding #3' situation report (6 October 2026, hosted on ReliefWeb): 'From 16 September to 6 October 2026, flooding was reported across 50 provinces, affecting 1,474,981 households (4,188,452 people), with 31 deaths reported. As of 6 October, flooding remains ongoing in 27 provinces and Bangkok, affecting 1,149,285 households (3,143,962 people)...Bangkok: Approximately 329,000 households / 700,000 people were affected by flooding, with 4 deaths reported.' This nationwide toll of 31 deaths exceeds and supersedes GDACS's narrower tracked total (6 deaths, 627 displaced, episode 57) and is adopted as the new confirmed national total, being the more current and comprehensive allowlisted figure.

description: Torrential monsoon rain has flooded Bangkok and central Thailand since mid-September 2026, prompting the capital's governor to declare all 50 districts disaster-affected areas. IFRC and the Thai Red Cross reported on 6 October 2026 that flooding since 16 September has killed 31 people nationwide and affected 4,188,452 people (1,474,981 households) across 50 provinces; as of 6 October, flooding remained active in 27 provinces and Bangkok, affecting 3,143,962 people (1,149,285 households), including about 700,000 people (329,000 households) in Bangkok, where 4 deaths have been recorded and water levels are decreasing. This nationwide toll supersedes GDACS's narrower tracked total of 6 deaths and 627 displaced. Forecasters warn of renewed heavy rain and increased dam discharge in the Chao Phraya basin from 9-13 October, which could raise river levels further in low-lying and riverside areas.

This figure supersedes GDACS's narrower tracked total of 6 deaths and 627 displaced (episode 57, window 18 August-3 October). Forecasters warn of renewed heavy rain and increased Chao Phraya dam discharge from 9-13 October, which could raise flood risk again in low-lying and riverside areas.

name: Bangkok Flood Disaster, Thailand

updates.text: IFRC and the Thai Red Cross's 6 October situation report, now hosted on ReliefWeb, put the confirmed nationwide toll at 31 deaths and about 3.14 million people (1.15 million households) still affected across 27 provinces and Bangkok, with a cumulative 4.19 million people affected since 16 September -- superseding GDACS's narrower tracked total of 6 deaths and 627 displaced.

GDACS's reporting window extended to 3 October (episode 57): displaced rose to 627 (from 569) nationwide; the confirmed death toll held at 6, and the event remains at Green alert. The narrative now also cites flooding reported in Ratchaburi Province.

Media reports (CGTN) said Bangkok floodwaters were receding and easing nationwide, with a reported cumulative toll of 24 deaths and about 3.19 million people affected since mid-September; authorities warned of possible renewed flooding from additional rain and dam releases expected 4-6 October. GDACS's tracked figures (6 deaths, 569 displaced) remain unchanged.
GDACS's reporting window extended to 28 September (episode 52): confirmed deaths rose to 6 (from 4) and displaced to 569 (from 169) nationwide; the event remains at Green alert.

GDACS's death toll rose to 4 (from 3) as its reporting window extended through 27 September; the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration opened 200+ shelters (about 4,200 evacuated), and the governor said the situation had stabilised with floodwaters expected to recede in 2-3 days.
